findings.reason: The original standalone captures contain no illustration. A paired planar section materially clarifies the central geometric dichotomy and its essential qualification: odd-dimensional data agreement is on a neighbourhood of the sphere, whereas the even-dimensional velocity kernel is nonzero in the open interior. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a claim that the original text failed to render.

diagram_math_checks.objects: At fixed x and t>0 with c>0, R=ct>0; the figures are planar sections of radial sets in R^n, not an assertion that n=2 in the odd case.
diagram_math_checks.check: Both panels mark centre x and an outward segment of length R. Caption identifies rho=|y-x|, the radial variable in Statement (ii). No morphisms, commutativity or graph relations are asserted.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Odd n>=3, sphere radius R and concentric annular neighbourhood.
diagram_math_checks.check: The solid circle has drawing radius 1.3; the shaded annulus extends from 1.05 to 1.55, strictly surrounding it. Thus the shaded set is a neighbourhood of the sphere, as in Statement (i) and proof 1.1. Label says neighbourhood agreement suffices. Caption expressly excludes the stronger pointwise sphere-trace claim. Ring boundaries are illustrative, with no prescribed physical thickness.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Even n>=2, open ball B_R(x) and velocity kernel K(rho,t).
diagram_math_checks.check: The disk is shaded up to a dashed radius-R boundary; caption explicitly excludes the boundary. Labels K(rho,t)!=0 for 0<=rho<R and K(0,t)!=0 follow from proof 1.3: K=b(c^2t^2-rho^2)^(-(2k-1)/2), b nonzero. Since c,t>0 and rho<ct, the base is positive and smooth; this justifies all interior labels including centre. No sign positivity is asserted, since b alternates with k.

Proof steps 1.1-3.1 and all Facts remain unchanged. The illustration adds no premise: odd dependence is proved by sphere means and derivatives; even interior dependence by differentiation under the integral and a bump with fixed-sign kernel. The rigorous proof is independent of the figure.
